I can independently reproduce a closely matching issue on Windows with OpenCode 1.18.19.

When multiple OpenCode instances have active agent/subagent work, the entire system becomes sluggish, including delayed typing in the TUI. With 3-4 OpenCode processes active, total CPU usage reached 87-100%; each OpenCode process used roughly 0.9-1.2 GB working set memory.

After restarting and leaving one OpenCode process, the same controlled tool-loop tests stayed responsive:
- OpenCode CPU averaged 5.6-6.4%, with peaks below 17%.
- Input lag was not observed.
- The test used both `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`, so the symptom does not appear to depend on one model provider.

**Update:** further A/B testing points to Zed’s integrated terminal on Windows as the primary cause. OpenCode remains responsive with the same workloads in Windows Terminal and VS Code, while system lag starts when Zed is launched even separately. Multiple OpenCode instances appear to amplify the symptom, but are not the root cause in my case.

Yes — OpenCode already follows the standard XDG base-directory environment variables. Set these **before OpenCode starts**:

```sh
export XDG_DATA_HOME=/media/usb/opencode/data
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/media/usb/opencode/cache
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/media/usb/opencode/config
export XDG_STATE_HOME=/media/usb/opencode/state
```

OpenCode appends `/opencode` to each value, so the example stores files under paths such as `/media/usb/opencode/data/opencode`.

The relevant variables are:

- `XDG_DATA_HOME` — the important one for backup growth: database/session data, logs, auth, snapshots, tool output, and managed repos/worktrees.
- `XDG_CACHE_HOME` — downloaded binaries and other rebuildable caches.
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — global OpenCode config, agents, commands, plugins, themes, etc.
- `XDG_STATE_HOME` — small persistent UI/model/plugin state.
- `TMPDIR` — optional; relocates temporary files too.

There are also narrower OpenCode-specific overrides:

- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=/some/directory` — relocate only the global config directory.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/some/opencode.json` — load a particular config file.
- `OPENCODE_DB=/absolute/path/opencode.db` — relocate only the SQLite database/history.

For this use case, setting the four XDG variables is the cleanest way to move everything while keeping each category separate. If only the backup size is the problem, `XDG_DATA_HOME` (and optionally `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) may be enough.

Existing files are not migrated automatically. Stop OpenCode, copy the existing directories, preserve ownership/permissions, then restart with the variables set. On Home Assistant, the USB path also needs to be mounted and writable inside the add-on/container; a host-only path will not be visible there.

## Triage: linked PRs do not address this issue

Cross-checking the PRs linked to this issue, **neither actually fixes the `structuredClone(part)` leak described here**:

### PR #42150 — targets a different bug
- Title: `fix(opencode): make text/reasoning delta accumulation O(N) instead of O(N²)`
- PR body says **"Fixes #30067"** (O(N²) text-delta accumulation in `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts`), not the `structuredClone` heap growth in `packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts` described in this issue.
- Different file, different root cause. The two issues are related (both session memory) but the fixes are independent.

### PR #35111 — the real fix, stale-closed
- Author is the issue reporter (`@xingruodong-sys`). Branch `fix/35107-memory-grows`. Title matches this issue. **Closed 2026-08-03 by the `github-actions` stale-PR bot** ("Automated PR Cleanup: >1 month old, <2 positive reactions"), not by a maintainer.
- It was not merged and not maintainer-rejected — it rotted due to inactivity.

### Net status
No merged or open PR currently addresses #35107. The issue is effectively **unowned** right now.

### Suggested next step
A maintainer should decide one of:
1. Reopen PR #35111 and review it (the one-line `structuredClone(part)` → `part` removal, guarded by confirming the projector in `session/projectors.ts` only destructures/inserts and never mutates `part`).
2. Accept a fresh PR from another contributor (the fix is a one-line removal; the issue body already proposes it).

I'm happy to open a clean PR if a maintainer confirms. Not opening one unilaterally to avoid duplicating #35111.

(Context: I hit this while investigating memory bloat in my own opencode sessions — reported in capsule oxmiq/capsule#1762. The `structuredClone` per-PartUpdated path is the strongest match for "many subagents + tokens = RSS growth" among the open upstream issues.)

## Triage: linked PR does not address this issue

Cross-checking the PR linked to this issue, **PR #38939 does not fix the AI-SDK Effect `EventTarget` leak described here**:

### PR #38939 — targets a different leak
- Title: `fix(core): prevent allBounded listener leak via PubSub subscription`
- PR body footer says **"Closes #36677"** (V2 PubSub `allBounded` leak in `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/event.ts` and `packages/opencode/src/share/share-next.ts`), not the AI-SDK Effect runtime `EventTarget` (`[vY]` in bundled `chunk-624361m2.js:25:4492`) described in this issue.
- Different leak path, different subsystem. The issue here is the bundled AI SDK Effect runtime; #38939 is the V2 PubSub core.

### Net status
No open or closed PR addresses #34574. The leak is in a **bundled/vendored AI SDK artifact** (`chunk-624361m2.js`), so a fix likely needs either:
1. An upstream AI-SDK dependency bump (if the listener leak is fixed in a newer SDK version), or
2. A wrapper in opencode that removes listeners after each LLM evaluation completes.

### Suggested next step
A maintainer should confirm whether #34574 and #36677 are considered duplicates (same symptom, different root cause) or distinct. If distinct, #34574 still needs a dedicated fix.

(Context: I hit this while investigating memory bloat in my own opencode sessions — reported in capsule oxmiq/capsule#1762. The AI-SDK EventTarget listener leak is one of the two strongest matches for "many LLM calls = RSS growth" among the open upstream issues, alongside #35107.)

"Herdr’s output here matches the Kitty keyboard protocol. Unless the pane requests Report all keys as escape codes (bit 8), unmodified Enter, Tab, and Backspace remain legacy bytes; modified Backspace can use CSI-u. Pane apps must keep accepting 0x7f/0x08, or request bit 8.

Making Herdr emit CSI-u without that request, or adding a passthrough policy, would change established input behavior rather than fix a protocol violation. I’m closing this as a feature request under the bugs-only intake. "

| Event | Agent default | Effective model |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Build turn | `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3#max` | `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3#max` |

This was the same primary session, not a delegated child. The agent changed, but the subsequent Plan turns retained the Build model and variant.

The current V2 implementation appears to model this as two independent operations:

- [`Session.switchAgent` and `Session.switchModel` are separate core operations](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e49772a8b4db867f638ffad9f7d188ccbbe05b58/packages/core/src/session.ts#L142-L146).
- [`switchAgent` publishes only the agent change](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e49772a8b4db867f638ffad9f7d188ccbbe05b58/packages/core/src/session.ts#L393-L402).
- [The protocol exposes separate endpoints](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e49772a8b4db867f638ffad9f7d188ccbbe05b58/packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts#L173-L200).
- [The agent-switch unit test asserts only the new agent](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e49772a8b4db867f638ffad9f7d188ccbbe05b58/packages/core/test/session-create.test.ts#L327-L332).
- [The client test explicitly performs both switches](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e49772a8b4db867f638ffad9f7d188ccbbe05b58/packages/client/test/effect.test.ts#L117-L124).

Suggested regression coverage:

1. An unpinned session switching A -> B atomically adopts the configured model and variant for B.
2. An explicitly pinned user model follows the chosen pinning policy across agent switches.
3. Use agent default clears the pin and adopts the current agent default.
4. No provider turn can observe new agent instructions and permissions with the previous agent model.

@rekram1-node I took a pass at the plugin approach you suggested.

I added two generic provider hooks to both the Effect and Promise plugin APIs:

- ctx.provider.hook("available", ...) lets providers using automatic activation determine availability from ambient authentication.
- ctx.provider.hook("model.prepare", ...) runs after catalog, variant, credential, and native-package mapping, but before URL validation and provider model construction. It can mutate the runtime modelID and settings.

Bedrock now owns its AWS behavior entirely inside AmazonBedrockPlugin. The plugin:

- Detects availability using the actual AWS default credential chain, including default shared profiles without AWS_PROFILE.
- Resolves profile, SSO, process, container, web-identity, and instance-role credentials before native model construction.
- Preserves explicit static credentials and Bedrock bearer API keys.
- Expands region-dependent endpoints from the effective configuration.
- Retries after credential-chain failures and periodically refreshes cached non-expiring credentials.


Basically retry logic is as follows for bedrock specifically:
- If credential resolution fails, the next attempt uses forceRefresh.
- If it returns temporary credentials from SSO, STS, credential_process, etc., those credentials usually include an expiration: Date. The AWS SDK automatically refreshes them when they are within five minutes of expiration.
- Static environment or shared-file credentials usually have no expiration, so the five-minute interval is intended to periodically reread them.
